cards.explanation: The answer is bronze. Goliath, the Philistine champion from Gath, wore a bronze helmet, a bronze coat of mail and bronze armor on his legs, and he carried a bronze javelin slung between his shoulders (1 Samuel 17:5-6). That's a lot of bronze, friends. I can't even get my oven mitts to match.

Goliath wants Israel to choose one man to come fight him. He shouts, "Choose one of your men and have him come down against me." It's one man against one man, friends. Then he lays out the stakes: the loser's side becomes the servants of the winner's side (1 Samuel 17:8-9).

The answer is True. Goliath says, "If he is able to fight me and kill me, then we will be your servants." That's the deal on the table, bakers. Then he adds the other side: if he wins, Israel becomes the servants of the Philistines.

The answer is that they're dismayed and greatly afraid. When Saul, king of Israel, and all the Israelites heard the Philistine's words, they were dismayed and greatly afraid (1 Samuel 17:11). That's the whole camp, friends, from the king on down. Goliath's challenge reached everybody.

The answer is youngest. Jesse, an old man from Bethlehem, had eight sons, and the text says David was the youngest (1 Samuel 17:12-14). His three oldest brothers had followed Saul. David was last in line, friends.

The answer is forty days. The text says, "For forty days the Philistine came forward every morning and evening to take his stand." Morning AND evening, bakers, for forty days. That's a man with a very reliable schedule and a very rude one.

The answer is False. Jesse, David's father, sends him with roasted grain, ten loaves and ten portions of cheese. He tells him, "Check on the welfare of your brothers and bring back an assurance from them." Nothing about bringing anybody home, friends.

The answer is True. David left his supplies in the care of the quartermaster and ran to the battle line (1 Samuel 17:22). Smart move, bakers. You don't want to be holding ten loaves and a pile of cheese when the action starts. Then he asked his brothers how they were doing.

The answer is that they flee from him in great fear. When all the men of Israel saw Goliath, they fled from him in great fear. That's the whole army, friends, not just one nervous soldier. David has just arrived and is standing right there watching it happen.

The answer is great riches and his daughter in marriage. The men of Israel said the king would give great riches to the man who kills Goliath, and he would give him his daughter in marriage (1 Samuel 17:25). That's the offer going around camp, friends. That's a very big prize.

The answer is True. The men said the king would also "…exempt his father’s house from taxation in Israel." That's the winner's whole family house, bakers, not only the winner. Riches, a royal marriage AND no taxes. Somebody in that camp must have done the math.

The answer is the armies of the living God. David asks, "Just who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?" Notice who David says is being defied, friends. He doesn't say it's just Israel's soldiers or the king. He says it's the armies of the living God.

The answer is False. When Eliab, David's oldest brother, heard him speaking to the men, his anger burned against David. He said, "I know your pride and wickedness of heart…" and David answered, "What have I done now?" (1 Samuel 17:28-29). That's how the text records it, friends.

The answer is False. The text says David turned from Eliab toward another man and asked about the offer again. Those people answered him just as the first ones had (1 Samuel 17:30). He kept on asking, bakers.

The answer is that David offers to go and fight Goliath himself. David tells Saul, "Let no man’s heart fail on account of this Philistine. Your servant will go and fight him!" (1 Samuel 17:32). Quite a day, friends, for a shepherd who was sent with supplies for his brothers (1 Samuel 17:17-18).

The answer is that Saul says David is just a boy and Goliath is a warrior. He says, "You cannot go out against this Philistine to fight him. You are just a boy, and he has been a warrior from his youth." Honestly, friends, I get where he's coming from. On paper, it's not a close matchup.

The answer is that David grabbed it by its fur and killed it. David says, "If it reared up against me, I would grab it by its fur, strike it down, and kill it." That's a shepherd who takes the job seriously, bakers. I flinch when a cookie sheet clangs, so I'm taking notes.

The answer is LORD. David says, "The LORD, who delivered me from the claws of the lion and the bear, will deliver me from the hand of this Philistine." Notice who gets the credit, friends. David looks back at what the LORD already did, and that's what he's counting on now.

The answer is False. David tried to walk in Saul's tunic and armor, and he told Saul, "I cannot walk in these…" and "I am not accustomed to them." So he took them off (1 Samuel 17:39). Sometimes you walk better in your own gear, friends.

The answer is sling. With the stones in his shepherd's bag, David took his staff in his hand and "…with his sling in hand, he approached the Philistine." A staff, a bag and a sling, bakers. That's the whole kit.

The answer is because he's just a boy. The text gives the reason right away: when Goliath looked at David, "…he despised him because he was just a boy, ruddy and handsome." (1 Samuel 17:42). He looked, he saw David, and he despised him, friends.

The answer is True. Goliath had just asked if he was a dog that David came at him with sticks (1 Samuel 17:43). Then he calls to David, "Come here," and says, "and I will give your flesh to the birds of the air and the beasts of the field!" (1 Samuel 17:44). That's the threat he makes, bakers.

The answer is that there is a God in Israel. David tells the Philistine, "This day the LORD will deliver you into my hand… Then the whole world will know that there is a God in Israel." (1 Samuel 17:46). What the world will know is about God, friends, not about David.

The answer is that the battle is the LORD's. David says, "…it is not by sword or spear that the LORD saves; for the battle is the LORD’s, and He will give all of you into our hands." He says it to all those assembled there (1 Samuel 17:47). The reason he gives, friends, is that the battle belongs to the LORD.

The answer is forehead. David "…took out a stone, and slung it, striking the Philistine on the forehead." Then the stone sank into his forehead, and Goliath fell facedown on the ground (1 Samuel 17:49). The text says David did it with a sling and a stone (1 Samuel 17:50). One stone, one shot, friends.

The answer is False. The text says, "…David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and a stone; without a sword in his hand he struck down the Philistine and killed him." There was no sword in his hand when it happened, bakers. The sword only came after, when David pulled Goliath's own sword from its sheath (1 Samuel 17:51).

The answer is False. The text says, "When the Philistines saw that their hero was dead, they turned and ran." No second champion, friends, and no new challenge. Then the men of Israel and Judah charged after them (1 Samuel 17:52).

The answer is to Gath and the gates of Ekron. The men of Israel and Judah pursued the Philistines "…to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron." Gath was Goliath's hometown, friends. Philistine bodies were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron (1 Samuel 17:52).

The answer is whose son he is. Saul says to Abner, the commander of the army, "Abner, whose son is this young man?" Abner answers, "As surely as you live, O king, I do not know." Even Abner's drawing a blank, bakers.
The answer is Jesse. Saul asks, "Whose son are you, young man?" and David answers, "I am the son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem…" (1 Samuel 17:58). That's the name David gives, friends.
